back: The way in which an action is performed, or (in plural form 'manners') polite social behavior. During the biology presentation, Marcus answered questions in a poised, respectful manner.
extra: Differentiate between the singular method of doing something and the plural social etiquette.

back: An individual's general mood, attitude, or mental outlook; can also refer to lively enthusiasm or team loyalty. Despite the rain dampening the football field, the students maintained high spirit during the homecoming pep rally.
extra: Disambiguate mental outlook ('high spirits') and collective enthusiasm ('school spirit') from supernatural entities.

front: In English class, Jordan analyzed how the main {{c1::character}} made tough choices under pressure.
extra: In English class, Jordan analyzed how the main character made tough choices under pressure.

back: The outward visual look of someone or something; can also denote the public arrival or emergence of an individual. Before entering the mock interview room, Sofia checked her appearance in the hallway mirror to make sure her blazer was buttoned.
extra: Clarify physical outward look versus formal public arrival or deceptive outward impression.

front: Biology was Maya's favorite {{c1::subject}}, especially during the laboratory unit on cellular division.
extra: Biology was Maya's favorite subject, especially during the laboratory unit on cellular division.

front: The history teacher explained how several 19th-century families built a vast {{c1::fortune}} during the industrial boom.
extra: The history teacher explained how several 19th-century families built a vast fortune during the industrial boom.

front: Mr. Alvarez awarded extra {{c1::credit}} to students who revised their lab reports.
extra: Mr. Alvarez awarded extra credit to students who revised their lab reports.

back: Past tense of observe: to watch something carefully with attention, to state a remark, or to comply with a rule. While conducting the chemistry experiment, the lab group observed the liquid turning from clear to dark blue.
extra: Note difference between scientific monitoring, making a verbal comment, and obeying a regulation.

back: To consider, gaze at, or evaluate someone or something in a specified way; as a noun, esteem, respect, or reference. The guidance counselor holds high regard for students who balance after-school jobs with homework.
extra: Clarify relational phrase ('with regard to') versus personal esteem ('high regard') and looking attentively.

back: Firmly determined on a course of action; alternatively, having settled or found a solution to a dispute or problem. After receiving feedback on her first draft, Priya resolved to outline every essay before writing.
extra: Distinguish firm internal decision-making from external conflict resolution.

front: Marcus had a sudden {{c1::fancy}} to try out for track even though he had never sprinted before.
extra: Marcus had a sudden fancy to try out for track even though he had never sprinted before.

back: Personal behavior in a public or institutional setting; as a verb, to direct, manage, or carry out a process. The student council code outlines expectations for personal conduct at school dances and sports events.
extra: Explain noun stress CON-duct (behavior) versus verb stress con-DUCT (lead, direct, transmit).

back: Having an excessively high opinion of one's own looks or abilities; alternatively, producing no positive result (futile). The student made a vain effort to finish the twenty-page reading packet ten minutes before class began.
extra: Clarify the idiom 'in vain' (useless/futile) versus personal conceit.

back: Showing good judgment, reason, and common sense; in older literary texts, capable of perceiving or feeling something. Packing an extra rain jacket for the outdoor field trip proved to be a sensible decision.
extra: Contrast practical wisdom ('sensible decision') with archaic perception ('sensible of the cold').

front: The principal's tone turned {{c1::grave}} as she addressed the high school assembly about online safety.
extra: The principal's tone turned grave as she addressed the high school assembly about online safety.

back: The quality of being amusing or comical; can also denote a person's temporary emotional mood or temper. When the sound system failed during rehearsal, the drama teacher used warm humour to calm everyone down.
extra: Distinguish wit/comedy from temporary emotional temperament and the verb 'to humour'.

back: A purpose, deliberate plan, or intention; alternatively, a visual layout or sketch created for a project. The robotics team adjusted the structural design of their mechanical arm to lift heavier weights.
extra: Contrast technical or artistic layout with deliberate intent or plot ('by design').

front: During the debate tournament, Maya kept a calm {{c1::countenance}} even when the opposing team made sharp objections.
extra: During the debate tournament, Maya kept a calm countenance even when the opposing team made sharp objections.

extra: The vice principal reminded the class that skipping detention carries a serious disciplinary consequence.
